question.problem: A fair six-sided die is rolled $10$ times. What is the standard deviation of the number of times we get an even number? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
Let the random variable $X$ be equal to the number of times we get an even number.

Here, we have the following information:

- there are $n=10$ rolls of the die

- the probability of getting an even number (i.e., a $2,$ $4,$ or $6$) on any roll of the die is

$$
p=\frac{3}{6}=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

So, $X$ follows a binomial distribution, where $X∼B(10,\frac{1}{2}).$

For a binomial random variable $X,$ the standard deviation is given by

$$
\text{SD}[X]=\sqrt{\text{Var}[X]}=\sqrt{np(1-p)},
$$

where $n$ is the number of experiments and $p$ is the probability of success on each experiment.

So, the standard deviation of the number of times we get an even number is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{SD}[X] & =\sqrt{np(1-p)} \\  & =\sqrt{10\cdot \frac{1}{2}\cdot (1-\frac{1}{2})} \\  & =\sqrt{2.5} \\  & =1.581\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
